extracted.intended_audience: NIH/AHRQ grant recipients (PD/PIs), Signing Officials (SOs), Administrative Officials and grants management staff preparing and submitting RPPRs and related Additional Materials (FRAM/IRAM/PRAM).
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and procedural/formatting requirements for completing the NIH Research Performance Progress Report (RPPR) including how to prepare and submit additional-materials requests (FRAM, IRAM, PRAM), Section A–I content expectations, and publication/product reporting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM response format and upload actions
rubrics_metrics.description: When a Program Official (PO) requests additional material related to the Final RPPR (FRAM), the PI can either upload an attachment meeting the requested information requirements or, for Revised Outcomes (Section I), enter/paste text into the Revised Outcomes text box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drag-and-drop or browse to upload files; the interface shows allowed file counts and types. After upload you may Download or Delete files using icons. The original request can be viewed via the Closeout Status > Status Information > Closeout Final Report Additional Materials Request link. Subsequent uploads are appended in the stored PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRAM submission responsibility and editability
rubrics_metrics.description: Only Signing Officials (SOs) may submit FRAM to the Agency. After the SO submits FRAM to the Agency, the FRAM cannot be edited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After PI uploads, the SO navigates to Closeout Status and uses the FRAM Update button; the FRAM screen shows a Submit button. Once submitted, Closeout Status shows FRAM Submitted By <SO Name>, a View link appears, and FRAM becomes uneditable. Email notifications are sent to submitting SO, PI, and PO. Note: the PO may rescind approval; if rescinded, FRAM Update becomes available again. SOs may add attachments even after submission (prior to Agency acceptance); subsequent documents are added to the Commons-generated PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRAM use and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim Report Additional Materials (IRAM) provides a mechanism to respond to IC Program Official requests following an Interim RPPR. A PD/PI (or Contact PI) can enter IRAM; only the SO can submit IRAM to the Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AHRQ award recipients do not receive or respond to IRAM requests. For Revised Project Outcomes on Interim RPPRs, follow the IRAM outcomes process (text box entry) rather than FRAM file upload used for Final RPPRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised Project Outcomes content, format, and public posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Outcomes describe cumulative outcomes/findings and will be made publicly available with the PD/PI name attached in RePORTER. For NIH awards, Outcome statements should not exceed half a page and the text field is limited to 2,000 characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcome statements must: be written for the general public in clear, concise, comprehensible language; be suitable for public dissemination (may be available electronically); not include proprietary, confidential information or trade secrets. The IRAM/FRAM interface shows a caption warning that text will be publicly available. See NIH notices NOT-OD-17-022 and NOT-OD-17-037 for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRAM upload limits and submission controls
rubrics_metrics.description: For IRAM (and other RAM requests), users may upload files or enter Revised Outcomes text and then use Cancel, Preview, Save, Delete, or Submit controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may upload up to 10 documents for IRAM. Cancel returns to Status without changes; Preview opens a view of uploaded documents and comments; Save stores uploaded content for future submission; Delete removes uploaded documents; Submit sends uploaded documents and Revised Outcome text to the Agency. Use Download/Delete icons to manage uploaded files before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRAM purpose and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency Requested Progress Report Additional Materials (PRAM) is used to respond to Grants Management Specialist (or AHRQ) requests for additional information following an RPPR. PD/PIs (or PD/PI Delegates) can initiate PRAM; the SO must submit unless the PD/PI has been delegated Submit Progress Report authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency-requested PRAM is not available for multi-year funded awards. The PRAM UI shows Grant Information and a section to add requested materials; up to 100 attachments may be submitted and all attachments must be PDF files.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRAM file type and quantity requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: PRAM uploads: up to 100 attachments allowed, and all attachments must be in PDF format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Drop Files area or browse to upload; Download and Delete icons are available for each uploaded file. The Additional Materials Requested by IC section updates to list uploaded files.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRAM routing workflow and reviewer actions
rubrics_metrics.description: PRAM can be routed to the next reviewer from the Route button; a drop-down lists available reviewers. A Comments field is optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When routing, select Next Reviewer, optionally enter comments, and submit. The Route action displays the PD/PI Assurance statement; reviewers must read and click Submit to agree. Routing updates status to Reviewer Work in Progress, sends emails to the PD/PI and the selected SO/Next Reviewer, and records routing history. After routing, PD/PI cannot edit unless the PRAM is routed back.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRAM recall rules
rubrics_metrics.description: PRAM routed to a reviewer can be recalled by the person who performed the routing action up until submission of the current attachment(s) to the Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The last reviewer can recall; Signing Officials at the organization and the Contact PD/PI who are not the last reviewer can also recall when status is Reviewer Work in Progress. PD/PI delegates cannot recall. Recalled PRAM status becomes PD/PI Work in Progress (if recalled by PI) or Reviewer Work in Progress (if recalled by SO); routing history and emails are updated. Only items not already submitted may be recalled; prior PRAM submissions remain unaffected.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRAM submission and SO certification
rubrics_metrics.description: When PRAM is in Reviewer Work in Progress status, the SO can submit it to the Agency (PD/PIs may submit only if delegated Submit Progress Report authority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before submitting, SO may Preview as PDF, Route to another reviewer, or View Routing History. On Submit, the SO must read a certification that the organization is in compliance with the Notice of Award and Grants Policy Statement and verify validity/accuracy, then click I Agree. After submission, status becomes Submitted and current reviewer updates to Agency; routing history is recorded and email notifications sent to PD/PI, submitting SO, SO assigned to RPPR, and AO assigned to RPPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission PRAM behavior and viewing
rubrics_metrics.description: After PRAM is submitted to the Agency, the Preview button remains but the ability to view or delete individual attachments is removed; uploading additional attachments remains possible until the award is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple PRAM submissions can occur; Preview shows only the latest submission. To view all submissions as one document, access Status Information and select the PRAM link. The generated PDF includes an information header for each PRAM submission followed by its attachments, with the most recent submission first and bookmarks for navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not include PII or PHI in the RPPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Do Not Include Personal Identifiable Information (PII) Or Protected Health Information (PHI) in the RPPR. Sensitive PII and PHI require strict handling and must not be included in RPPR submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of sensitive PII: Social Security Number, personal financial information, Alien Registration Number. Examples of PHI: personal medical conditions. Documents containing sensitive PII or PHI must not be included. NIH-specific FAQs and IC Privacy Coordinators provide additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section A – Cover Page data and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Section A includes award, PD/PI, organization, and project/reporting/budget period information; many fields are pre-populated from eRA systems and Commons Profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To update contact info (addresses, emails, phones) edit Commons Profile and save. Select Signing Official (SO) and Administrative Official (AO) from dropdowns (they may be the same person). The SO who submits need not be the one selected. Recipient ID is optional and ignored by the Agency. UEI replaced DUNS as official entity identifier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact PD/PI change rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If Contact PD/PI changes (multiple-PD/PI awards only), indicate change in Section A and enter the new Contact PD/PI Commons ID. The change does not take effect until the Agency accepts the report and issues a Notice of Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new Contact PD/PI must have PD/PI role in eRA Commons and be associated with the recipient organization. The RPPR is not an appropriate vehicle for prior approval to change/add/delete PD/PIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section B – Goals (B.1) reporting expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: List major goals of the project as stated in the approved application or as approved by the Agency. If milestones/target dates exist, identify them and show actual completion dates or percent complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goals = specific aims. Generally goals do not change; if Agency approved changes occurred during the reporting period, list revised goals and explain significant changes in approach/methods. Significant changes in objectives/scope require prior Agency approval. Specific aims must be provided in the initial RPPR; subsequent RPPRs pre-populate aims and may be amended only when allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section B – Accomplishments content and length (B.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe for the reporting period: (1) major activities; (2) specific objectives; (3) significant results (major findings, developments, conclusions, positive and negative); and (4) key outcomes or achievements. Include discussion of goals not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As project progresses, emphasize accomplishments over activities. Emphasize significance of findings to the scientific field and include approaches used to ensure robust and unbiased results. For most NIH awards limit the response to no more than 2 pages. If citing references provide full citations. List products separately in Section C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section B – Reporting Revisions/Supplements (B.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any Revision/Supplement requires reporting, identify each by grant number or title and describe the specific aims and accomplishments for each funded Revision/Supplement during the reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Award (NoA) will indicate reporting requirements; the NoA also incorporates NOFO requirements that may include reporting components. Use Add/New to populate tables for revisions/supplements. For SBIR/STTR awards specific aims and accomplishments are equivalent to aims/milestones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section B – Training and professional development reporting (B.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe opportunities for training and professional development provided to anyone who worked on or participated in activities supported by the project during this reporting period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If research is not intended to provide training or there is nothing significant, select Nothing to Report. Training includes mentoring, courses, one-on-one mentoring; professional development includes workshops, conferences, seminars, etc. For projects reporting graduate students/postdocs in Section D, describe whether Individual Development Plans (IDPs) were established — do not include actual IDP documents. For awards designed for training (T, F, K, R25, R13, D43, etc.) a response is required; follow supplemental instructions and do not duplicate Section B accomplishments. Limit to this reporting period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section B – Dissemination to communities (B.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how results have been disseminated to communities of interest, including outreach to communities not usually aware of the research to enhance public understanding or interest in science careers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine dissemination (e.g., websites, press releases) need not be reported. If the award is not designed to disseminate information or conduct outreach, select Nothing to Report. Detailed responses are required only for award components designed for public dissemination/outreach. Scientific publications and sharing of research resources are reported under Products (Section C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Section B – Plans for next reporting period (B.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly describe what you plan to do during the next reporting period to accomplish the goals and objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss efforts to ensure scientific rigor and unbiased results. Significant changes in objectives/scope require prior Agency approval. Include important modifications to original plans and provide scientific justification for changes involving human subjects or vertebrate animals; describe such changes in Section F. Not applicable for Interim and Final RPPRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR progress-report special instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: For SBIR/STTR awards, progress reports should include a one-page abstract describing the research plan; for Fast-Track and Phase II include an updated commercialization plan as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include these items in the RPPR as directed and ensure they are limited to the reporting period where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section C – Products: which works to report
rubrics_metrics.description: Section C collects publications and other products arising directly from the award during the reporting period. Report only publications that were accepted/made public during the reporting period and that directly arise from the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Product types are not mutually exclusive; select a primary product type and assign additional types as applicable. Publications listed elsewhere in the RPPR (e.g., cited in B.2) will not be automatically tracked as award products unless associated in C.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and interim research products: expectations for claiming
rubrics_metrics.description: Preprints and interim research products may be reported if they are publicly available and directly result from the award. To claim an interim product, NIH expects the recipient has made it publicly available and recommends use of a CC-BY license or public-domain dedication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the document text: acknowledge NIH funding per NIH Grants Policy Statement Chapter 8.2.1; clearly state the work is not peer-reviewed; declare any competing interests as an author would. Publications not peer-reviewed are not covered by the NIH Public Access Policy. Recipients are responsible for public access compliance of publications listed in C.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to omit publications from C.1 (non-personnel-only contribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the award's only contribution to a publication is non-personnel resources (materials, equipment, data), the recipient should not list the paper in C.1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such publications may be listed in Section B.2 (accomplishments) but will not count against B.2's two-page limit and will not be tracked as a product of the award; the recipient is not responsible for ensuring public access compliance for such papers listed only in B.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to report publications via My NCBI and RPPR behavior on publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication data in RPPR C.1 tables is drawn from the PD/PI's My NCBI and My Bibliography and is dynamic until the progress report is submitted; upon submission the publication data is frozen in the progress report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are three tables: (1) All Publications Associated with this Project in My NCBI (auto-checked 'Associate with this RPPR'); (2) Publications Not Associated with this Project in My NCBI (can be associated by checking box); (3) Publications Previously Reported for this Project. Leaving 'Associate with this RPPR' checked associates publication with the RPPR, displays it in RePORTER, and makes association permanent in My NCBI and PubMed; unchecking disassociates it. The NIH Public Access Compliance column shows compliance status from My NCBI; recipients are responsible for compliance even for previously reported items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting RPPR with non-compliant publications - notification and remediation expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications that fall under the NIH Public Access Policy and are non-compliant must still be reported. The system will send an automated email requesting evidence of compliance or an explanation by a due date (two weeks prior to next budget start date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PD/PIs should take steps to bring non-compliant publications into compliance promptly because compliance issues can affect award renewal timeliness. See My NCBI manage compliance guidance and NIH Public Access resources.
